topic.title: Multiplication
topic.description: A path to multiplication for a child who needs smaller steps: equal or not, make them equal, counting in groups and moving from addition to the multiplication sentence. The child answers by tapping, without words; the app changes levels by itself as the child succeeds.
equal_check.title: Equal?
equal_check.methodology: The child looks at two plates and answers with “Equal” or “Not equal”. After a right answer it appears in big letters on the table. After a mistake — “Look again”, the child can answer again and the next task is easier. Levels: A – a difference of two or more; B – a difference of one; D – each plate scattered differently, so the child compares amounts, not patterns. Up a level – 8 of 10 right first time.
equal_check.settings: “Automatic” starts from the last level reached and changes it by itself. A chosen level stays fixed for the whole lesson.
equal_check.params.level.label: Level
make_equal.title: Make them equal
make_equal.methodology: The child moves items between groups until they are equal: by dragging, or by tapping “from” and then “to”. We do not say how many each – the child finds it. There is no “Check” button: once equal, everything lights up. In the first task a hand shows how to move an item. Hints grow: 6 seconds without a move or 2 moves the wrong way – the fullest group blinks; then an arrow “from → to”. Wrong moves are not blocked. Levels: R – two groups, one move, hint at once; A – no hint; B – two moves; C – three groups; D – 3–4 groups.
make_equal.settings: “Automatic” starts from the last level reached and changes it by itself. A chosen level stays fixed for the whole lesson.
make_equal.params.level.label: Level
skip_count.title: Counting in groups
skip_count.methodology: The bridge from counting in ones to multiplication. The child taps the groups in order; above each group appears how many so far: 3, 6, 9. Levels: R – the number appears by itself and the voice counts (a model); A – choose from two numbers; B – from three, groups of 3 and 4; C – earlier numbers fade, keep the count in mind; D – groups of 2–5, up to 5 groups. Start with 2s and 5s. From level B the groups vary: plates, boxes. Wrong options are typical mistakes (added one item instead of a group, off by one). After a mistake the items are counted on one by one from the previous number.
skip_count.settings: “Automatic” starts from the last level reached and changes it by itself. A chosen level stays fixed for the whole lesson.
skip_count.params.level.label: Level
sum_to_product.title: Addition → multiplication
sum_to_product.methodology: The child taps the groups and the sum “3 + 3 + 3 + 3” builds up. Under each addend its number appears (1, 2, 3, 4) – this shows where the number of groups in the sentence comes from. Then the sum folds into a multiplication sentence with small pictures under the numbers (how many in a group, how many groups). Order and sign follow the school of the chosen language. Levels: R – build and watch; A – point to “how many in a group” and “how many groups” in the sentence; B – the same without building, faint pictures; C – fill in the missing number.
sum_to_product.settings: “Automatic” starts from the last level reached and changes it by itself. A chosen level stays fixed for the whole lesson.
sum_to_product.params.level.label: Level
sum_to_product.params.level.option.C: C – fill in the missing number
